Fair conditions are expected across much of the Marianas through 
this evening. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are 
expected to develop over Saipan and Tinian coastal waters late 
tonight as TD 31W barrels northwestward, with the current forecast 
taking it north of Agrihan. However, 31W's motion, and position north
of an attendant trade-wind trough, will drag a col area over the 
islands tonight, leading to light and gentle winds through at least 
early Saturday morning. Winds will likely become light and variable 
at times. Tinian and Saipan are expected to see only the outermost 
rainbands associated with TD 31W, and these may end up somewhat 
limited in coverage given its rapid northwest movement. Convection on
the far south-southwest periphery of 31W is currently moving into 
northeastern Saipan coastal waters. For more information on TD 31W,
see the Tropical Systems section below.

A fairly dry trade-wind regime looks to resume by Sunday morning, and
continue through the coming week. Low-end scattered showers and
isolated thunderstorms are possible from time to time with weak 
transient trade-wind troughs, especially around Sunday night.

Marine/Surf...
Light to moderate north to northeast trade winds will shift
tonight as TD 31W moves across the far northern CNMI, becoming 
northwest for Tinian and Saipan, and east for Guam and Rota. The 
passage of 31W will drag a col area across the Marianas, and winds 
likely become light and variable at times tonight. Then, there will 
be a shift to light to moderate south to southeasterlies Saturday, 
before trade winds return Sunday. Scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms move across Tinian and Saipan tonight, mainly across 
the northern coastal waters. Combined seas of 5 to 7 ft will begin to
decrease Saturday, becoming 4 to 6 ft Saturday night through Sunday 
night, before increasing a foot or so Monday. Seas are comprised of 
an elevated northeast trade swell and a lighter long-period north 
swell, which are reinforced by the approach and passage of TD 31W
through the far northern CNMI. This is sufficient to generate a high
risk of rip currents along north and east facing reefs, and 
hazardous surf along north reefs tonight and Saturday, before swells
and surf subside Saturday afternoon. A High Surf Advisory for north 
facing reefs, and a High Rip Current Risk for north and east facing 
reefs have been issued through 4 PM ChST Saturday.

Tropical Systems...
Newly-formed Tropical Depression 31W is centered east of the 
northern CNMI near 18N148E, or 160 miles east of Pagan, 275 miles 
northeast of Saipan, or 400 miles northeast of Guam. 31W is a 
lopsided storm with most of its convection along the west and 
northwest flanks, barrelling northwestward toward the northern CNMI 
at 21 mph. Maximum sustained winds are at 30 mph, focused mainly 
north of the center. TD 31W will move through the northern CNMI
tonight, passing to the north of Agrihan early Saturday morning,
potentially as a tropical storm. However, the current forecasted
tropical storm wind field is expected to remain along 31W's northern
flank, away from Agrihan, as it moves quickly away Saturday morning. 
However, this could change if 31W develops faster, or shifts farther 
south than its current forecast suggests. Residents of the northern 
CNMI should continue to monitor forecasts and bulletins for any 
changes to these expectations. 

For more information on Tropical Depression 31W, see bulletins 
issued by JTWC under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and by the National
Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Eastern Micronesia remains fairly dry this evening, with only patches
of scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms, mainly near Pohnpei
and south of Majuro. Scattered showers will move through Pohnpei
later this evening through tonight, becoming isolated again Saturday
morning. By Saturday night, the Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) is
expected to become a bit more active, first over Pohnpei, then
spreading east to Kosrae and Majuro by Sunday morning. This will not
be a large rain producing increase, with POPs (Probability of
Precipitation) not increasing higher than 30 percent. Convection will
clear out of the Marshalls by Sunday evening, then at Kosrae and
Pohnpei Monday night or Tuesday. 

No changes made to the marine forecast. Benign seas with mostly light
to gentle winds are expected through the beginning of next week.

Western Micronesia...
For Palau and Yap, a relatively dry trade-wind regime will continue
through Sunday afternoon, with light to gentle northeasterlies and 
isolated showers in the forecast. Then, a surface trough extending
from an embedded circulation within the NET will intensify on Sunday
night. Both Palau and Yap should expect gusty winds, isolated
